entries.answer: David Izuchukwu Gilbert is a Chemical Engineering student at the University of Lagos (300 Level) and a self-taught software developer based in Lagos. He builds web products and applied AI features, independently and in small teams.
Selected work: Swift, GraphSense, Vouch, PayPal Hub, Fraud Detection. There are 16 projects in the full archive, covering software, applied AI and engineering competitions.

Software: React, Next.js, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, Tailwind CSS, Vite, Node.js, Express, FastAPI, Python, REST APIs. Data and backend: PostgreSQL, Supabase, Firebase, Firestore, Prisma ORM, Git and GitHub. Machine learning: pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, Random Forest, SMOTE, Hugging Face Transformers, LoRA, mT5. Engineering: ANSYS, MATLAB, JMP, AutoCAD, Fusion 360, Blender, RTsim.Career; mass and energy balances, heat transfer, process control fundamentals.
Available for freelance projects. SIWES placement at Nigerite ended on 3 November 2026. The quickest way to start is a message on WhatsApp or email.
Email: israelizuchukwu17382302@gmail.com. WhatsApp and phone: +234 706 834 9199. He is based in Lagos, Nigeria.
The Master CV is a PDF with education, projects, experience, awards and skills.

B.Eng. Chemical Engineering, University of Lagos (2024 to 2029 (expected)). Now in 300 Level. Official CGPA 4.65/5.00 through 200 Level, first semester; second-semester results pending. Recipient of the NNPC/Seplat 2026 National Undergraduate Scholarship (Seplat Energy PLC). Senior Secondary Education, Elite Crop College (2020 to 2023). Overall Best Graduating Senior Secondary School Student and Head Boy, 2023. SAT 1360/1600, JAMB UTME 302/400 (2024), WAEC three A grades, NECO five A grades.

SIWES Trainee, Process Department (SM6), Nigerite Limited (1 Sep to 3 Nov 2026). Contributor, Academic and Competitions Team, AIChE UNILAG (Nov 2026 to present). NextGen AI Hackathon, Team Participant, Wale Lab (Nov 2026). AI Upskilling Programme, Selected Participant, FATE Foundation and Google DeepMind (Africa AI Upskilling Programme) (Nov 2026 to present). GCI World 2026 September Programme, Matsuo-Iwasawa Laboratory, University of Tokyo (Sep to Dec 2026 (ongoing)). AI/ML Fellow, 3 Million Technical Talent (3MTT), Cohort 4 (2026 to present).

Scholarship recipient: NNPC/Seplat 2026 National Undergraduate Scholarship, Seplat Energy PLC. 1st place: GraphSense, AFRETEC-UNILAG MathWorks category. Top 20 of 300+: Dangote Cement Plc University Engineering Challenge 2026 (team leader). 4th of 10 teams: PIDEC 1.0, Klova (team leader); Stage 1 score 90.5/100. Top 20 semifinalist: The Industry Discourse 5.0 Energy Startup Challenge (team leader). 63rd of 1,600: Squad Hackathon 3.0, Vouch.
David's graphic design work lives on a separate site. Those pieces are self-initiated concepts, and the photography in them is licensed stock.
David takes on focused websites and frontends, web apps with accounts and data, and applied AI features. He explains his part, what has been tested and what still needs work.
Projects are labelled by what they are: team projects state David's part, concepts are marked as concepts, and no client results are claimed.

Swift (Education platform, 2026). An academic platform for UNILAG engineering students combining structured course materials, testing and AI-assisted question generation. Role: Owner · full-stack developer. Independently rebuilt and maintain the platform across the frontend, authentication, database, course-material workflow, quiz system and AI-assisted question-generation backend. Result: Several students.

CrxRay (Developer tooling, 2026). A developer-focused project built for the Tech Literacy Network Hackathon, designed around making technical systems easier to inspect and understand. Role: Hackathon project. Worked on the product as part of the hackathon team, including implementation and preparation of the working demo and submission. Result: TLN Hackathon 2026.

Vouch (Financial reputation, 2026). A portable trust profile for informal businesses that turns transaction behaviour into a clearer financial-reputation signal. Role: Frontend engineer · hackathon team. Built the trader-facing interface, including the dashboard, score visualisation, tier progression and live server-sent-event updates. I did not build the scoring model or the entire product. Result: 63rd of 1,600 · Squad Hackathon 3.0.

PayPal Hub (Hackathon product, 2026). Find it, pay with PayPal, keep your subscriptions in check. A PayPal AI Hackathon product with a Guardian that watches subscriptions. Role: Frontend engineer · hackathon team. Contributed to the frontend: the homepage, authentication experience, discovery interface and supporting screens, with reusable components. A team handled the backend and AI functionality separately. Result: PayPal AI Hackathon 2026.

Point of Grace Ministries (Church website · Indianapolis, 2025). The website of Point of Grace Ministries, a church in Indianapolis, USA. Role: Website maintainer and manager · family church. Maintained and managed the site through 2025 for my uncle's church. It was handed to a new developer at the start of 2026, so the live site today is their version, not mine. It was not a paid agency engagement. Result: Maintained through 2025.

entries.answer: Urban Brand Creatives (Business website, 2026). A website for a Nigerian creative agency, designed and built end to end as a frontend portfolio project. Role: Frontend designer and developer · independent project. Designed the interface and built it in React and Next.js. It is a portfolio project, not a live client deployment, and no lead results are claimed. Result: Frontend design project.

Resonance (AI product intelligence, 2026). A two-agent product-intelligence system for product rating and audience segmentation. Role: Frontend engineer · four-person team. Built the frontend interface and implemented Firebase Authentication and Firestore persistence for the team product. Result: Authentication + persistence.

NexStore (Storefront frontend, 2026). A working storefront frontend with sample products, search, category filters and a persistent bag. Prices and checkout are not connected. Role: Frontend developer · solo project. Built the browsing and bag interactions. Further pages and functional improvements are in development. Result: Frontend demo, in progress.

Pepper Table (Restaurant website concept, 2026). A responsive Nigerian restaurant website concept with a sample menu, search and category filters. No operating restaurant or orders are implied. Role: Frontend developer · solo project. Built the multi-page static frontend and menu interactions with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Result: Independent website concept.

Commonwell Church (Church website concept, 2026). A four-page website concept for an imagined church community, including first-visit information and sample community pathways. Role: Frontend developer · solo project. Built the responsive pages and interactions. The congregation, location and programme details are illustrative. Result: Independent website concept.

GraphSense (Engineering visualisation, 2026). A MATLAB prototype translating chart data into changing audio pitch, developed during the AFRETEC-UNILAG MathWorks bootcamp. Role: Team Sync · MATLAB project. Developed the MATLAB implementation and demonstration video for Team Sync, based on Mumeen’s original concept. The web beta is a separate work in progress. Result: 1st place · UNILAG MathWorks bootcamp.

Fraud Detection (Applied machine learning, 2026). A comparative machine-learning study for detecting fraudulent card transactions in a highly imbalanced dataset. Role: ML engineer · ECX project. Engineered features, applied SMOTE, compared classification models and evaluated performance on a separate test set. Result: 568K transactions · 99.97% recall.

Multilingual news classification (Language models, 2026). Topic classification and headline generation for Hausa, Igbo, Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin. Role: DSN bootcamp hackathon participant. Experimented with mT5 and LoRA fine-tuning, compared simpler baselines and prepared competition submissions. Result: mT5 and LoRA experiments.

Cement mill analysis (Process engineering, 2026). Mill-shell and liner analysis for the Dangote Cement Plc University Engineering Challenge. Role: Team leader · Team Kilvora. Led ANSYS structural and thermal analysis, supporting calculations and technical research with a two-person team. Modelled conversion estimates are not plant results. Result: Top 20 of 300+ submissions.

TLUD cookstove (Clean-energy concept, 2026). A design-stage gasifier cookstove and pay-as-you-go adoption concept. Role: Team leader · Team Axel. Led a four-person team and reviewed fuel, market and financial assumptions. No deployed stove or sales are claimed. Result: Top 20 semifinalist · TID 5.0.

Klova (Process engineering, 2026). A gravity-fed biofiltration cartridge designed and tested by Team CHG for PIDEC 1.0. Role: Team leader · Team CHG. Originated the concept and led the six-person team through design revisions, prototype work and testing; created two Blender process visualisations. Result: 90.5/100 Stage 1 · 4th of 10 national finalists.
